citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. XVII, p. 756, Fig. 387
claim_text: The skulls of Dimorphodon and Pteranodon are related by coordinate transformation.
quote_printed: In Fig. 387, a, we have the skull of Dimorphodon, and in Fig. 387, b, that of Pteranodon. ... The two co-ordinate systems are superposed in Fig. 387, b; and it is seen that the transformation of the one into the other is of a simple kind.

equations.E0: All vendored inputs SHA-256 pinned in inputs_sha256; script fails closed on mismatch
equations.E1: phi : R^2 -> R^2 orientation-preserving (det D phi > 0 on the form domain)
equations.E2: phi_t(x) = (1 - t) x + t phi(x), homotopy from identity to the Dimorphodon->Pteranodon grid map
equations.E4: Thin-plate spline (Bookstein 1989) fitted on cranial landmarks + semilandmarks: phi(P_dim) = P_pte
equations.E5: Affine least-squares control: Q ~ [1 P] M
equations.E7: t* = <D - A, B - A> / |B - A|^2 for best-fit stage along the warp segment

state_variables.P_dim: Landmark configuration on Dimorphodon skull outline (Fig. 387a, Cartesian grid)
state_variables.P_pte: Corresponding landmarks on Pteranodon skull (Fig. 387b, oblique grid)

boundary_conditions.grid_a: 8 x 4 Cartesian grid on Dimorphodon (Thompson Fig. 387a)
boundary_conditions.correspondence: Orbit + four cranial process tips + equal arc-length semilandmarks between tips

parameter_regime.role: coarse semilandmarks, exact TPS at anchors
